_about: Ideas killed in the second kill pass on 25 Oct by a separate reader, with its reasons. Never build the board from this file.

wed.killed: virus idea removed: biology-adjacent, tripped the model safety filter; do not re-offer
wed.so_what: An AI has designed a medicine that was given to a person, and its maker has not said whether it worked: when anyone shows you what their AI designed, ask what was proven outside the computer, and what is being kept back.

fri.from: The inspiration sweep (sources you follow), 24 Oct
fri.so_what: Eight in ten CIOs are spending more on AI, and only about one in eight says it has paid off in a big way: before you approve next year's AI budget, ask which one team will use it deeply enough to change how it works.
fri.story: Gartner's surveys this week: 81% of CIOs are raising AI spend while 13% say they have seen significant value. Andrej Karpathy describes the same gap from the other end: a few thousand people use AI at full depth while most only ask a chatbot quick questions. The pattern: the value is going to depth of use, and money alone does not buy it.
fri.why_now: Gartner published the survey data at its IT Symposium/Xpo, reported on 21 October 2026.
fri.fact: Gartner: 81% of CIOs are increasing AI spend; 13% of CIOs say their organizations have realized significant or transformational value from AI; 11% of CFOs see clear returns.

source.label: The Deep View, 21 Oct 2026, on Gartner's surveys

beats: Hook: 81% spending more, 13% seeing much for it.
Thread one: the CIOs and CFOs, in Gartner's own numbers.
Thread two: Karpathy's sharp funnel, the few who use AI at full depth and the billions who barely do.
The pattern: the gap is depth of use, which money alone does not buy.
A dated call on next year's Gartner figure.

experiment.why: Your Hannah Fry card: a warm, lit talking head explaining one surprising number, close to camera.

fri.so_what: The soap opera is the first screen format AI is taking over, and the people who own characters are buying the teams who make them: if you own stories or characters, decide this quarter whether you make AI series yourself or license them to someone who will.
fri.story: Character.AI was making short AI dramas you could talk back to, and Disney is now hiring most of its team. China's short-drama film sets emptied this year as studios switched to AI, and an AI-made series app reports paying subscribers at almost the same rate as its filmed one. The pattern: short drama is where AI-made shows earn first.
fri.why_now: Court filings reported on 19 October 2026 show Disney offering jobs to 66 Character.AI staff after its bankruptcy.
fri.fact: Character.AI had begun a push into original microdramas this summer; court filings show Disney looking to hire 66 Character.AI employees at $60 million a year for three years.

source.label: Gizmodo, 19 Oct 2026, citing the court filings and Bloomberg

beats: Hook: the soap opera on your phone may not have a single actor in it.
Thread one: one Chinese producer went from about 200 shoots a month to about 30 as studios switched to AI (Sixth Tone, August).
Thread two: an AI-made series app turns viewers into payers at almost the same rate as its filmed one (industry report, July; check at the fact gate).
Thread three: Character.AI's talk-back dramas, and Disney hiring the team that made them.
A dated call on the first big Western studio to release an AI-made series.

experiment.why: Build the piece like a vertical drama itself: cliffhanger cuts between the three threads.

reasons.virus (wed): No 200-person media, adtech or data business builds or buys a phage, so it fails the under.the.hood reader; its so_what changes how the reader thinks (mind.the.gap ground); its build lesson is a closing moral. Biology-adjacent: it also tripped a model safety filter. Never re-offer.
reasons.gartner (fri): A CIO survey is the dull enterprise subject Krish ruled out on 6 Oct; its so_what changes a budget (follow.the.money ground); the Karpathy thread had no dated source, so only one thread; a familiar story told straight instead of turned around.
reasons.soap opera (fri): Its fact and why-now (Disney hiring 66 Character.AI staff) are the same headline as Friday idea 1, thread two; its other threads are from July and August; Gizmodo says "original microdramas" and "looking to hire", not "talk-back dramas" or "hiring"; make-or-license is a build or contract decision.
